source: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, speech at Nagpur, 26 December 1941
edition: Jamil-ud-din Ahmad, Some Recent Speeches and Writings of Mr. Jinnah, Lahore: Sh. Muhammad Ashraf, January 1942
evidence_type_and_verification: Contemporary primary speech collection; page images checked
relevance: Direct attack on Savarkar and Moonje and their recruitment policy; links Hindu military control with denial of an independent Muslim state
limitation: A hostile characterization of their plan, not independent proof of its practical success.

source: A. S. Bhide, From Quit India to Split India
edition: Poona: Manohar Mahadeo Kelkar, 1945; foreword by N. C. Kelkar
evidence_type_and_verification: Contemporary Mahasabha account quoting a Muslim newspaper; pages checked
relevance: Chapter X reproduces Eastern Times criticism of wider recruitment and Hindu/Sikh militarisation; chapter dated February 1943
limitation: Original Eastern Times issue/date/byline not recovered. Bhide’s own conclusions must be distinguished from the newspaper quotation.

source: M. R. T. [Muhammad Sharif Toosy], Pakistan and Muslim India
edition: Bombay: Home Study Circle, with foreword by M. A. Jinnah; first published 1942 according to Dhulipala; accessible copy catalogued 1945
page_locator: 14, 32, 212–213; p.32 is PDF image 47; p.212 is image 226
evidence_type_and_verification: Pro-Pakistan primary polemic; p.32, p.212 and foreword checked
relevance: Fears loss of privileged northwestern military representation under Hindu predominance; explicitly criticises Savarkar’s militarisation appeals
limitation: The p.32 subject is Muslims AND Sikhs of the northwest. Do not silently turn the combined recruitment share into a Muslim-only statistic.

source: M. R. T., Nationalism in Conflict in India
edition: Bombay: Home Study Circle; contemporary companion volume
evidence_type_and_verification: Contemporary pro-Pakistan primary polemic; OCR searched
relevance: Argues that Britain would lose the help of Muslim recruiting areas if it alienated the League
limitation: Accessible scan/text has discontinuities around this passage. Used as supporting evidence, not for an extended exact quotation.

source: V. D. Savarkar, Campaign to Fan Up the Martial Spirit in the Hindu Race, 6 October 1941
edition: Historic Statements by Savarkar, edited by S. S. Savarkar, 1967
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary statement in a later collection; complete relevant pages inspected
relevance: Explicitly seeks a dominant Hindu position in the armed services and identifies existing Muslim predominance as the condition to change
limitation: Proves stated intention; its claims about actual representation require separate statistical verification.

source: V. D. Savarkar, Cawnpore presidential address, December 1942
edition: Hindu Rashtra Darshan, collected presidential addresses; digital edition
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary address in a collected edition; relevant pages inspected
relevance: Anti-Pakistan resistance is directly followed by a programme to intensify Hindu military recruitment and reduce the Muslim share
limitation: The often repeated 62-to-32 figures are the speaker’s claims. They are not necessary to establish his intention.

source: Alan Campbell-Johnson, Mission with Mountbatten
edition: 1951 edition in the accessible scan
evidence_type_and_verification: Participant diary account; page image checked
relevance: Records Liaquat’s complaint about inadequate Muslim representation and request for immediate reorganisation to facilitate division
limitation: Entry does not name Savarkar. It cannot establish that his campaign caused the complaint.

source: Rajendra Prasad, खण्डित भारत
edition: Banaras: Gyanmandal, 1946 scan; author of India Divided
evidence_type_and_verification: Contemporary Hindi reproduction of Sikandar Hayat Khan’s scheme; p.294 image checked
relevance: Clause 18 preserves communal proportions in the peacetime army at their 1 January 1937 level, with an emergency exception
limitation: Sikandar’s federal proposal is not equivalent to Jinnah’s demand for a sovereign Pakistan, nor a response to Savarkar’s wartime campaign.

source: Vijaykumar Pujari, कांग्रेस-लीग और हिन्दू महासभा
edition: Delhi: Ratan & Co.; title page says first edition December 1946
evidence_type_and_verification: Contemporary Hindi political advocacy; title and relevant page images checked
relevance: Explains recruitment into army, navy and air force as military training for Hindu benefit, rather than altruistic aid to Britain
limitation: Useful for contemporary reception and explanation of purpose. It supplies no independently checked League objection in the inspected military chapter.

source: V. D. Savarkar, समग्र सावरकर वाङ्मय, खंड ८
edition: Collected Marathi works, post-independence account of the Abhinav Bharat concluding ceremony
evidence_type_and_verification: Savarkar’s retrospective Marathi account; page image checked
relevance: Claims deliberate growth of the Hindu share of the forces and discusses training and future use of arms
limitation: Retrospective testimony by the policy’s author; not contemporary evidence of a particular Muslim leader’s reaction.

source: Dhananjay Keer, Veer Savarkar
edition: Second edition, 1966
evidence_type_and_verification: Sympathetic secondary biography; OCR and notes checked
relevance: Reports Ziauddin Ahmad’s alarm at Poona; identifies Eastern Times and cites Bhide p.27; cites Campbell-Johnson for Liaquat
limitation: Ziauddin report lacks a recovered date and original speech report. Eastern Times and Keer are one citation chain, not two independent witnesses.

source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina
edition: Cambridge University Press, 2015
evidence_type_and_verification: Scholarly secondary study; PDF searched and relevant sections read
relevance: Traces Jinnah’s support for Toosy’s books and their Urdu translation; discusses military arguments for Pakistan
limitation: The p.163 paraphrase is less precise than Toosy p.32 about the combined Muslim/Sikh recruitment share.

source: Ayesha Jalal, The State of Martial Rule
edition: Cambridge University Press, 1990
evidence_type_and_verification: Scholarly secondary study citing a primary letter
relevance: Cites Liaquat to Mountbatten, 7 April 1947, Transfer of Power X p.152, for Pakistan’s need for its own army
limitation: Underlying Transfer of Power document not independently recovered in this pass.

source: Qalb-i-Abid and Massarrat Abid, Muslim League, Jinnah and the Hindu Mahasabha
edition: Journal of the Research Society of Pakistan 45(1), 2008
evidence_type_and_verification: Scholarly corroboration
relevance: Reproduces and contextualises Jinnah’s Nagpur attack on Mahasabha militarisation
limitation: Prefer the verified January 1942 primary collection for exact quotations.

source: Stanley Wolpert, Shameful Flight: The Last Years of the British Empire in India
edition: Oxford University Press, 2006
page_locator: 47; chapter 3 notes 49–50 cite Transfer of Power II pp.956, 958
evidence_type_and_verification: Scholarly secondary account with precise primary reference
relevance: Jinnah’s 13 September 1942 press conference invokes his claimed Muslim army share and international Muslim support in the Pakistan discussion
limitation: Underlying Transfer of Power text not independently checked here. Treat the percentage as Jinnah’s claim, not a verified army return.

source: H. S. Suhrawardy and Tamizuddin Khan, Bengal Home Guard debate, 21 September 1942
edition: Bengal Legislative Assembly Proceedings, volume LXIII, part 1
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary legislative debate; critical page images checked
relevance: Suhrawardy alleges exclusion of Leaguers and consultation with the Hindu Mahasabha; Tamizuddin opposes coercive Home Guard enrolment and defends League National Guards
limitation: Objections to alleged partisan arrangements; the scheme officially admitted both communities. Original circular not independently recovered.

source: Firoz Khan Noon to Jinnah, 12 April 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993
page_locator: Document 312, p.527; F.399/164–165; zero-based PDF page 753
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary private letter in official documentary edition; page checked
relevance: Fears British delay will hand the army to Hindus; demands a decision on Pakistan
limitation: Concerns control of the army rather than a named recruiting campaign.

source: Raghib Ahsan to Jinnah and Suhrawardy, memorandum package, 13 April 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary submitted memoranda and letter; critical images checked
relevance: Fears Hindu control of military resources; proposes Muslim counter-mobilisation and 30,000 Muslim ex-servicemen for Bengal armed police
limitation: Ahsan’s submissions are not evidence of Jinnah’s endorsement or official adoption.

source: Mirza Ahmad Ispahani to Jinnah, 28 April 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary private letter; page images checked
relevance: Urges expanding Punjabi police and eliminating the Gurkha force as a political danger
limitation: Police composition rather than explicit criticism of Savarkar; author is Mirza Ahmad, not Hassan Ispahani.

source: H. S. Suhrawardy to Liaquat Ali Khan, 21 May 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993
page_locator: Enclosure 1 to document 479, pp.867–871, especially p.870; F.458/75–79
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary private letter; date and military passage checked
relevance: Complains that troops sent to Bengal are Hindu and would work against them in a struggle over Bengal’s future
limitation: Allegation about local deployment, not a validated description of the whole army.

source: M. A. Hassan Ispahani to Jinnah, 16 March 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary private letter; heading and critical paragraph checked visually
relevance: Demands investigation into reported formation of separate Hindu and Sikh regiments while Muslim-containing regiments remain mixed
limitation: Records his alarm, not independent confirmation of his unnamed informant’s allegations or alleged Congress coup.

source: Firoz Khan Noon, public demand reported 4 April 1947
edition: Hasan-Askari Rizvi, Military, State and Society in Pakistan, 2000; cites The Statesman, 4 April 1947
page_locator: p.52; note 53 on p.255; PDF pages 69 and 272 (one-based)
evidence_type_and_verification: Scholarly secondary report with precise contemporary newspaper citation; book pages checked
relevance: Demands partition of forces, ordnance factories and equipment before independence because army control determines power over India
limitation: Original newspaper not recovered; report date is not independently established speech date. Different occasion from Noon’s 12 April private letter.

source: Liaquat Ali Khan to Mountbatten, 13 April 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993; also Transfer of Power, volume X, document 135
page_locator: Annex V to document 420, pp.758–759; letter No.26-P.S.F.R./47; Transfer of Power X pp.220–221
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary follow-up letter; date and passage checked on images
relevance: Fears Hindu control will prevent later creation of a balanced Pakistan force; asks for Muslim representation and a partition plan
limitation: Distinct letter in the same exchange as the already covered 7 April complaint; not independent corroboration. Running heading May must not override the letter’s April date.

source: M. Ziaud Din to Jinnah, enclosing an unnamed Muslim army officer’s memorandum, 19 April 1947
edition: Z. H. Zaidi, ed., Jinnah Papers: Prelude to Pakistan, 20 February–2 June 1947, first series, volume I, part I, National Archives of Pakistan, 1993
page_locator: Document 330 and enclosure, pp.571–576; F.472/18 and F.472/19–22
evidence_type_and_verification: Primary covering letter and anonymous memorandum; critical page images checked
relevance: Objects to proposed dilution of the Baluch Regiment’s Muslim share; urges League intervention and a public campaign
limitation: Officer unnamed; forwarder a barrister, not authenticated as Sir Ziauddin Ahmad of AMU. Statistics and accusations not independently verified.

source: Nawab Muhammad Ismail Khan, dissent on armed-forces nationalisation, reported May 1947
edition: Hasan-Askari Rizvi, Military, State and Society in Pakistan, 2000; cites The Statesman, 22 May 1947
page_locator: p.52; note 52 on p.255; PDF pages 69 and 272 (one-based)
evidence_type_and_verification: Scholarly report with contemporary newspaper locator; book pages checked
relevance: Objects to military nationalisation planning that ignores partition
limitation: Original dissent and newspaper not recovered; no verbatim quotation attributed to him; no explicit Savarkar or Hindu recruitment link.
